assertions.text: Discount ladder, and traveller eligibility are in separate tables. Rolling window counting as a third table is desirable.
assertions.evidence: The response provides three tables: `reisDiscountTier`, `discountByPassengerType`, and `discountedTicketPrice`. The third table tests price application arithmetic, not rolling window boundary counting. No separate table exists for rolling window testing (e.g., boundary at 30 vs 31 days).

assertions.text: Children's flat 20% discount is represented — either as a row in the eligibility table or a separate note. It does not follow the ladder.
assertions.evidence: In `discountByPassengerType`: 'Child, infrequent | CHILD | {0, 3, 4} | 20' and 'Child, frequent | CHILD | {5, 20, 40} | 20' show the 20% discount regardless of trip count, and @Description states: 'Children always receive a flat 20% discount regardless of trip count.'

assertions.text: The discount ladder has multiple tiers derived from the 'every fifth trip' rule, with boundary values or value sets showing which ticket counts produce which discount. The maximum 40% discount is represented.
assertions.evidence: `reisDiscountTier` shows multiple tiers with value sets: '{5, 6, 7, 8, 9} | 5', '{10, 11, 12, 13, 14} | 10', through to '{40, 45, 100} | 40', representing the ladder structure and maximum discount.

assertions.text: The 30-day rolling window boundary is tested: a ticket at exactly 30 days is included, at 31 days is excluded.
assertions.evidence: No table exists dedicated to rolling window boundary testing. The tables mention 'Trips in last 30 days' in column headers but provide no separate test table with boundary cases (e.g., testing difference between 30-day and 31-day windows).

assertions.text: Eligibility uses human-readable values (yes/no or equivalent) rather than raw true/false. TypeConverter or similar mechanism mentioned.
assertions.evidence: The code uses PassengerType enum values (CHILD, ADULT, SENIOR) which are readable, but the response explicitly states 'TypeConverter or similar mechanism mentioned' — the response does not mention TypeConverter at all, only the enum usage.

assertions.text: Value sets in the tier table contain exactly the values that produce the same discount. No cross-tier contamination.
assertions.evidence: In `reisDiscountTier`, each tier's value set is distinct with no overlap: '{0, 1, 2, 3, 4} | 0', '{5, 6, 7, 8, 9} | 5', continuing through '{40, 45, 100} | 40', with clear tier boundaries.

assertions.text: The discount ladder table uses value sets for the ticket count column to group counts within the same tier (e.g. {5, 9} for min/max → 5%) — not one row per boundary value. The 'every fifth trip' rule creates tiers; the table should express tiers, not enumerate boundaries.
assertions.evidence: `reisDiscountTier` uses value sets like '{5, 6, 7, 8, 9}' and '{40, 45, 100}' to group counts within tiers, not enumerating one row per count or using min/max notation.

assertions.text: The tier-to-discount mapping is expressed once — not repeated across multiple tables. A price application table (if present) should test the arithmetic (base price × discount → final price) without re-enumerating which ticket counts map to which tier.
assertions.evidence: The tier-to-discount mapping is defined once in `reisDiscountTier`; `discountByPassengerType` and `discountedTicketPrice` test other concerns without re-enumerating the full ladder structure.

assertions.text: @DisplayName is present on test methods, OR method names read as clear descriptive titles when converted from camelCase/snake_case.
assertions.evidence: All three methods have @DisplayName: '@DisplayName("Reis discount tier")', '@DisplayName("Discount by passenger type")', '@DisplayName("Discounted ticket price")'

assertions.text: @Description is present on at least the class or the tier method and provides context beyond what the table rows already express — such as the discount ladder structure, eligibility rules, or application context. Does NOT merely restate the column names or summarise what the rows show.
assertions.evidence: All three methods include @Description with contextual information: first describes 'Every 5 tickets advances one tier (+5%). The first discount applies from ticket 5. Maximum discount is 40%', second explains eligibility branching, third explains pricing formula.

assertions.text: TypeConverterSources is used for at least one human-readable conversion (yes/no, or rolling window notation).
assertions.evidence: The response does not mention TypeConverter, TypeConverterSources, or any converter implementation. No code shows conversion from boolean or numeric values to human-readable strings.

assertions.text: Annotations appear in order: @DisplayName (if present), @Description (if present), @TableTest — not any other order.
assertions.evidence: All three methods follow the correct order: @DisplayName, @Description, @TableTest (e.g., '@DisplayName(...) @Description(...) @TableTest(...)')

assertions.text: If @Description is present and the text is longer than a single short line, it uses a text block (triple-quoted string """), not string concatenation with +. Passes if @Description is absent.
assertions.evidence: All @Description annotations use triple-quoted strings: '@Description("""...""")', not string concatenation with '+'.

assertions.text: The eligibility/passenger-type table includes a Zone column (or equivalent) with a value set to show that the discount applies regardless of zone — rather than silently omitting zone. The requirement explicitly says 'regardless of the zones you travel in'.
assertions.evidence: The `discountByPassengerType` table has columns 'Scenario | Passenger type | Trips in last 30 days | Discount?' with no Zone column to demonstrate zone irrelevance.

assertions.text: Adult and senior are expressed as a value set {ADULT, SENIOR} (or equivalent) in at least one row of the eligibility table, since they follow identical discount rules. Not enumerated as separate rows with the same outcome.
assertions.evidence: In `discountByPassengerType`, Adult and Senior are separate rows: 'Adult, below first tier | ADULT | {0, 1, 4} | 0' and 'Senior, below first tier | SENIOR | {0, 1, 4} | 0', not combined as a value set {ADULT, SENIOR}.

assertions.text: All 9 discount tiers are represented in the ladder table: 0% (tickets 1-4), 5% (5-9), 10% (10-14), 15% (15-19), 20% (20-24), 25% (25-29), 30% (30-34), 35% (35-39), and 40% (40+). Not just a subset of tiers.
assertions.evidence: `reisDiscountTier` includes all 9 tiers: 'Below first tier | {0, 1, 2, 3, 4} | 0', 'First tier | {5, 6, 7, 8, 9} | 5', through 'Maximum tier | {40, 45, 100} | 40'.

assertions.text: Each tier in the discount ladder is expressed as a single row with a value set for ticket counts — not split across multiple rows (e.g. separate rows for 'tier kicks in' and 'tier holds'). One tier = one row.
assertions.evidence: In `reisDiscountTier`, each tier is a single row: 'First tier | {5, 6, 7, 8, 9} | 5', with one value set per row, not split across multiple rows.

assertions.text: The rolling window table expresses time relatively (e.g. '14 days ago', '30 days ago', or an integer 'Days ago' column) rather than using absolute dates, making the table readable without needing to know the reference date.
assertions.evidence: No rolling window table is provided. The tables reference 'Trips in last 30 days' in column headers but do not have a dedicated table testing the rolling window boundary with relative time notation.
